Adds two BPF selftests that verify passing a read‑only map value pointer or a PTR_TO_MEM with MEM_RDONLY flag to a global BPF function/kfunc is rejected, confirming kernel enforces read‑only checks.
Adds a standard sysfs "label" attribute for ChromeOS EC sensors when their physical location is known, removing the custom "location" attribute and the associated field in the driver state.
Updates the LX2160A ARM64 device‑tree CAN node, correcting the `fsl,clk-source` property to use the proper uint8 encoding (`/bits/ 8 <0>`), which removes a warning about an overly long value.
The commit updates the MAINTAINERS file to add Roman Gushchin as a co‑maintainer for the memory controller subsystem.

The patch changes libiscsi so that the iscsi_cls_conn sysfs entry is created only after the iscsi_conn structure’s dd_data is initialized, preventing a NULL pointer dereference when userspace reads attributes. It also deletes the now‑unused iscsi_create_conn() helper.
The patch changes a cast in drivers/mmc/host/mxcmmc.c to first cast the pointer to uintptr_t before converting to enum mxcmci_type, eliminating a clang -Wvoid-pointer-to-enum-cast warning.
Extends can_changelink() check to recognize struct can_priv::bitrate_const, allowing netlink configuration of CAN devices with fixed bit rates without needing a no‑op do_set_bittiming callback.
Adds cleanup on the error path of xhci_alloc_stream_info() by calling xhci_free_stream_ctx() to free the allocated stream_ctx_array, eliminating a memory leak.
Adds a NULL‑pointer check after ioremap() in the ray_cs driver, handling cases where ioremap fails and preventing later dev_dbg from dereferencing a NULL pointer.

Fixes a memory leak in vsock_connect() where multiple non‑blocking connects could schedule the same delayed work, causing an extra sock_hold without a matching sock_put. Replaces schedule_delayed_work() with mod_delayed_work() and balances the reference count.
Converts the existing I2C binding for Atmel/Microchip SoCs from the legacy text format to the new Device Tree JSON‑schema format, updating the dt‑bindings repository accordingly.
Moves the LCOUNT constant definition for Intel SoundWire from the source file into a dedicated header, cleaning up hidden code and making the definition visible to other modules.
The patch modifies map_block() to set the block‑id handle only when get_hw_block_id() succeeds, avoiding returning handle 0 on failure.
Adds a missing WARN_ON validation for the vsi->vf pointer in ice_vsi_rebuild, fixing a kernel warning that occurred during VF reset after a prior change stored the VF pointer.
Removes dead DMA‑32 fallback configuration in the hisi_sas SCSI driver, simplifying the code because a 64‑bit dma_set_mask never fails when the mask is present.

The commit updates the armada_37xx watchdog driver’s .set_timeout callback to also write the new timeout value to hardware counter 1, which was previously unchanged, ensuring that ioctl(WDIOC_SETTIMEOUT) correctly changes the watchdog timeout.
The patch removes the .is_enabled flag from PRCMU clock drivers because the generic clock core already tracks enable counts, eliminating redundant state.

The patch reorganizes XIP‑related #ifdef blocks in the RISC‑V memory initialization code, moving the pt_ops macro next to its conditional and grouping similar XIP macros to reduce scattered CONFIG_XIP_KERNEL checks.

The patch relaxes the restriction on changing the SCSI target driver’s database root directory, allowing the change only when no devices are registered, fixing the previous inability to reconfigure dbroot after module load.
Adds cleanup of a legacy kprobe_event when add_kprobe_event_legacy() or attach fails, preventing stale tracefs entries left after a failed kprobe attach, especially when livepatch and kprobe coexist.
Adds remoteproc driver support for MediaTek mt8186's SCP, enabling the kernel to manage that remote processor.
Adds module parameters to the speakup_dummy driver so default driver settings can be supplied at boot, allowing configuration via module options instead of changing sysfs variables after boot.
Adds the legacy compatible string 'riscv,clint0' to the SiFive CLINT timer dt-binding so that QEMU‑generated device trees pass dt‑validate.

The patch adjusts swiotlb_max_mapping_size() to factor in the minimum alignment mask, correcting the calculation of the maximum DMA mapping size when the original buffer offset is non‑zero, which fixes boot failures on Hyper‑V Isolation VMs with forced swiotlb.
Updates the habanalabs driver to use the new unified memory manager for the command‑buffer flow, adding required code and deleting the previous memory‑management implementation.

The patch changes vmbus_request_addr() to return VMBUS_RQST_ERROR when the transaction ID is zero, preventing a NULL dereference in netvsc_send_completion() and aligning zero‑ID handling with Hyper‑V semantics.
The patch updates the i.MX JPEG driver to handle changes in the source resolution at runtime, refining the relevant function to support dynamic resolution adjustments.
The patch changes bpf_selem_alloc to use copy_map_value instead of memcpy, preventing user‑supplied data from overwriting the zero‑initialized spin lock field in BPF storage maps.

Fixes a race in MPTCP ADD_ADDR handling by caching the remote address earlier and using the cached value after releasing the PM lock, preventing overwriting when multiple ADD_ADDR options arrive consecutively.

The commit separates the device‑tree binding schema for the Synopsys DW uMCTL2 DDR controller from the unrelated Zynq A05 DDRC controller, updating the synopsys,ddrc-ecc.yaml file and related device descriptions.
The commit modifies the ARM64 Rockchip device tree for ROCK Pi 4 to set the I2S1 controller status to disabled, ensuring its pins remain usable as GPIO by default.
Adds definitions for the ADC block’s clock and reset lines in the Renesas r9a07g043 CPG driver, enabling the kernel to manage the ADC’s clock and reset.

The patch deletes the declaration and assignment of the variable 'mdss' in drivers/gpu/drm/msm/msm_drv.c because the code that used it was removed, eliminating a clang -Wunused-but-set-variable warning.

The patch changes tcp_v4_rcv() to call kfree_skb_reason() instead of kfree_skb(), adding specific drop‑reason codes (NO_SOCKET, PKT_TOO_SMALL, TCP_CSUM, TCP_FILTER) so that skb free events are logged with the reason.
The patch removes an obsolete comment and an unnecessary overflow check in mm/writeback because a prior commit guarantees the variable cannot be negative or overflow.

Updates the MAINTAINERS file to correct a broken reference caused by a prior conversion of Mediatek JPEG dt-binding to YAML and expands the entry to also cover the encoder YAML, ensuring maintainer lookup works.
The commit modifies the xfs_buf_incore() function to return an error code and place the buffer pointer in an output parameter, matching the style of other XFS buffer APIs.
Fixes the DSC slice reset logic in AMD DRM driver so that when neither min nor max slices can accommodate the pixel clock, DSC is correctly disabled.
Adds clock and reset definitions for PWM channels 8‑14 in the Renesas r9a09g011 CPG driver and marks the shared APB clock as critical to keep it always on.

The patch corrects FDMA handling for LAN966x when the MTU changes by reading the correct hardware MTU (including L2 header and FCS) and adjusting skb allocation to reserve space for skb_shared_info, preventing allocation failures.
The patch introduces bookkeeping data and code so the host can unwind the hypervisor stack in non‑protected nVHE mode, preparing for later stacktrace support.
Corrects a misspelled word in the error log printed when devm_snd_dmaengine_pcm_register() fails in the Microchip SPDIF receiver driver.
The patch sets the fb_modifiers_not_supported flag in the virtual KMS (vkms) driver so GDM3 does not attempt to use framebuffer modifiers, fixing the start‑up failure on virtual displays.
Corrects the Chinese translation of the devicetree item 'machine_desc' by keeping the whole word untranslated in the docs.
Adds a helper function in the pmbus hwmon driver to test whether a block register exists, because existing byte‑register checks fail when PEC is enabled.
The patch replaces the multiline macro vt6655_mac_word_reg_bits_off in the vt6655 driver with an equivalent static inline function, because the kernel checkpatch tool rejects multiline macros.
The commit corrects indentation and block‑quote formatting in the sysfs‑fs‑erofs ABI documentation to eliminate Sphinx warnings during HTML documentation generation.

The patch updates the Realtek rtw89 driver for the 8852c chipset, adding extra initialization for the BA CAM version 1 and fixing the host‑to‑controller (H2C) data layout to match the hardware expectations.
Adjusts whitespace/indentation in dcn32_hwseq.c to fix a smatch warning about inconsistent indenting, with no functional code changes.

Updates the ASoC jz4740-i2s driver to handle separate TX and RX FIFO flush bits on newer SoCs, flushing each FIFO independently before activation, correcting the previous behavior where only the TX flush bit was set, leaving the RX FIFO uncleared.
Enables QUP and GPI DMA nodes in the sm6350-lena device tree, preparing the board for future I2C functionality.
The commit adds PCI device IDs for Intel Raptor Lake PCH‑S LPSS to the mfd driver, enabling the kernel to recognize this new hardware.
The commit edits a comment in the crypto n2 code, deleting a duplicated word "to" to clean up the documentation.
The patch adds a USB audio quirk for the Accuphase DAC-60 to enable native DSD playback up to DSD256 by selecting the appropriate alternate setting, which was previously unsupported.
Adds support for the VCN 4.0 IP block in the amdgpu driver, providing its initialization and decoder/encoder ring functions.
Adds EXPORT_SYMBOL statements for MediaTek VCodec decoder power‑management functions so they are visible to other modules when the decoder is built as a loadable module.
Adds READ_ONCE to reads of net->ipv4.sysctl_igmp_qrv in IGMP code to prevent concurrent modification races.
Adds a boolean rx_timeout flag in the 8250 DW UART IRQ handling code to make the timeout condition explicit; no functional behavior change.

The patch updates the PTP OCP driver to check the return value of nvmem_device_find, which can be a valid pointer or an IS_ERR() error pointer, and adds proper error handling to avoid dereferencing a bad pointer.

The patch renames the kernel macro for ID_AA64MMFR2_EL1.VARange from the historic LVA name to the official name defined in the ARM DDI0487H.a specification, aligning kernel code with the spec without altering behavior.
The commit updates comments in the rzg2l thermal driver: replaces an unclear label with a clearer one, corrects a spelling typo, and moves a block comment to its own line to follow coding style.
The patch edits a source comment in powerpc/pseries/vas, removing a duplicated word "the" on line 807; no code logic is altered.
The patch deletes the unused variable `cnt` from recv_func in the r8188eu driver, cleaning up dead code.
The patch adds handling for failure to acquire a hardware semaphore in release_swfw_sync, logging an error and exiting to avoid an infinite loop when hardware is surprise‑removed.

The patch moves the call to maybe_wait_bpf_programs() out of the loop in generic_map_delete_batch, so the synchronize_rcu() barrier runs only once before returning to userspace, eliminating redundant synchronization per deletion.

The commit rewrites the KVM self‑test state_test to create a single vCPU via vm_create_with_one_vcpu() / vm_recreate_with_one_vcpu(), passing a struct kvm_vcpu instead of a global VCPU_ID, and switches to vcpu_run(). It removes the arbitrary non‑zero ID and simplifies test setup.

The patch replaces #ifdef CONFIG_PM_SLEEP guards in the vf610 IIO DAC driver with calls to pm_sleep_ptr(), allowing the compiler to omit the functions when CONFIG_PM_SLEEP is disabled, simplifying the code and avoiding propagation of this pattern to other drivers.
The commit updates the copyright year range in the maple_tree test code, extending it to cover the current development year. It modifies only comment/license text, with no functional code changes.
The commit updates the rc5t583 multi-function device driver to use the newer i2c .probe_new() callback instead of the older .probe, because the driver does not need the i2c_device_id argument.
The patch modifies vchiq_get_state in the vchiq_arm driver to add a NULL check and return early, also tidying the code for clearer readability.
Moves the efi32_pe_entry function from the assembly file head_64.S into the .text section, preparing it for extraction into a separate compilation unit.
The patch moves two CEC register definitions from the public header into adv7511_cec.c, eliminating unused‑variable warnings when the CEC driver option is disabled.
Adds CLK_OPS_PARENT_ENABLE flag to pixel and byte clock sources in the Qualcomm dispcc-sm6350 driver so that set_rate can succeed, fixing a failure in clock rate programming.
The commit updates the pcm3168a ASoC driver to replace legacy bus‑clock defines with the newer ASoC DAI format terminology, aligning the code with current naming conventions.

Adds a runtime validation that the number of IPA commands in a transaction does not exceed the TLV FIFO size and checks channel direction by passing a new flag to gsi_channel_data_valid() and using a local variable.
The commit removes a non‑bit‑field that follows a bit‑field in a packed struct, eliminating unwanted padding that altered the struct size used for zero‑ing and configuration calculations.

The patch fixes a bug in the Ocelot driver where moving a VCAP filter writes an outdated hit counter back to hardware, inflating statistics. It now reads the current counter into tmp->stats.pkts before migration, ensuring correct counters for self‑tests.
The patch deletes a conditional block in the NFS code that checks IS_SWAPFILE, because the macro is always defined, making the code dead. The change simply removes this unnecessary hack.
Updates the tps65219 regulator driver to use .is_enabled() for state checking in tps65219_set_bypass, fixing an incorrect enable test, and removes an unused ret variable.

Adds a transaction ID field to the IPA driver to track the first completed but unpolled transaction, updates it during NAPI polling, and includes temporary sanity‑check warnings that are later removed.
Deletes the now‑unused tstamp pointer from the mlx5e_txqsq struct in the mlx5e driver, after timestamp handling was migrated to the core driver.
The patch modifies the nxp-nci NFC driver to stop printing a spurious "header length mismatch" message when an I2C operation fails, returning only the I2C error code.
Adds device‑tree binding entries for the WCN6750 Wi‑Fi chip to expose Wake‑on‑Wireless (WoW) support via the ath11k driver, enabling the kernel to configure and use WoW on that hardware.
The patch removes the use of the global ARCH_NR_GPIOS macro in the GPIO aggregator driver, introducing a local constant set to 512 as the maximum number of GPIOs to aggregate.
The patch re-formats comments in the r8188eu driver to follow the drivers/net coding style, ensuring they match kernel conventions before the driver is merged.
Adds device‑tree binding definitions for the Renesas RZ/G2L interrupt controller, introducing the compatible string and required property specifications for kernel support.
The patch changes the return type of PS_RDY_CHECK in the r8188eu driver to the boolean type, reflecting that it only yields true or false.

The patch adds a guard in gfs2_glock_dq() to detect if a GL_ASYNC glock holder has already been removed from the active/waiting list, preventing a race where the holder could be dequeued twice after a failed async lock request.
The patch removes the driver‑specific yesno() helper in drm/amd/display and replaces its usage with the generic str_yes_no() from linux/string_helpers.h, updating includes accordingly.

The commit corrects an out-of-bounds array access in the imx-jpeg driver that occurs when JPEG parsing fails and an uninitialized slot index (MXC_MAX_SLOTS) is used, preventing kernel panic on module reload.
Adds device‑tree compatible strings for DH electronics i.MX8M Plus DHCOM and PDK2 boards to the ARM DT bindings YAML file, documenting these SoM/evaluation boards.

The patch corrects translate_desc() in vhost by preserving the original 'last' address when looping over IOTLB lookups, fixing a range mis‑calculation that could cause incorrect descriptor translation.
The patch adds a check in lib/cmdline's next_arg function to only read args[i-1] when i > 0, preventing an out‑of‑bounds memory access that caused a kernel page fault when parsing a quoted argument.
The patch reorders static functions and variables in the via686a hwmon driver to eliminate four unnecessary forward declarations, improving source layout and removing redundant code.

The patch changes acpi_processor_get_platform_limit() to compare the new _PPC value with the previously stored one and only update the frequency QoS request when it differs. It also validates the _PPC value against the state count and sets a consistent default QoS value in acpi_processor_ppc_init().
The patch deletes the build‑system logic that forced a special link order for arm64/head.o, relying on the linker script to place the required .head.text header correctly.
The patch modifies the Tegra194 PCI driver to compute the RAS DES PCIe capability offset at runtime instead of using a fixed hard‑coded value for each controller.

The patch modifies ASoC soc-pcm backend state handling for PAUSE_RELEASE, adding a per‑FE boolean to track pause state and changing the transition from STOP to PAUSE when all streams are paused, improving resource management.
Adds kernel support to record each unloaded module that introduced a taint, maintaining a list and count; feature is optional and disabled by default.
Blocks the /proc/powerpc/ofdt interface from altering the in‑kernel device tree when kernel lockdown is enabled, preventing untrusted changes that could bypass lockdown.
The commit updates ADI ASoC drivers to use the new legacy_dai_naming flag instead of non_legacy_dai_naming, aligning the drivers with the new naming flag convention for CPU‑side DAIs.
The patch changes a memory allocation in the ptp_ocp driver from kzalloc(x*y) to kcalloc(y, x) to use the overflow‑checking variant, which is more appropriate for allocating an array.
The patch removes the redundant regs pointer from coredump_params and relies on task_pt_regs(current) directly, simplifying core dump code.
Adds a dma_release_channel() call in emac_probe() error path to correctly free a DMA channel obtained by emac_configure_dma(), fixing a resource‑leak bug.
The patch modifies btrfs_ioctl to obtain the inode directly from the file descriptor and reuse that inode for subsequent callbacks, avoiding creation of a new inode instance.
Updates the i2c SCMI driver to replace a manual extraction of match data with the standard device_get_match_data() call in acpi_smbus_cmi_add(), improving code clarity and correctness.
Adds a helper rdev_mdlock_deref() that wraps rcu_dereference_protected() for rdev/replacement pointers accessed while mddev_lock is held, annotating these accesses to silence sparse warnings.
Implements handling of GTP_ECHO_REQ packets by sending a GTP_ECHO_RSP with the required IE, making the kernel GTP device conform to the GTP specification.

Adds a null‑pointer check before accessing hdev->name in Bluetooth logging helpers (bt_dev_info, bt_dev_warn, bt_dev_err, bt_dev_dbg) to prevent dereferencing an invalid hdev and causing kernel faults.
The patch replaces uses of cpumask_next_* with cpumask_first_* when the start index is -1 (i.e., beginning of mask) for efficiency, and introduces a missing cpumask_first_zero() helper.
The commit disables the clevo-mail LED driver by marking it as broken until the hardware interface for setting blink rate via brightness is corrected.
Adjusts nl80211 BSS lookup handling: if the lookup returns an error pointer, the code sets the BSS pointer to NULL before freeing, preventing an invalid free.

The commit changes the Aquantia PHY driver to clear default advertisements of 2.5 Gbps and 5 Gbps when the Ethernet port is limited to 1 Gbps, ensuring the PHY only advertises up to 1000BASE‑T as requested via phylink.
Adds missing rcu_read_lock and takes a reference to real_dev in bond_ethtool_get_ts_info() to protect against calls via setsockopt that lack RCU protection, fixing a crash reported by syzbot.
Adds logging for GPIO and DMIC quirks in the Intel SOF ES8336 ASoC driver, extending the previously logged SSP quirk to expose these quirks via kernel logs.
Renames the variables maxpctksize and maxpcktsize in the USB gadget UAC2 driver to the correctly spelled wMaxPacketSize, fixing inconsistent naming.
The commit modifies perf's data conversion to JSON so that tracepoint (probe) variables are emitted as "field name": "field value" entries using tep_print_field, fixing the previous omission.
The commit corrects typographical errors in warning and debug messages within the nvmet-auth subsystem, changing string literals to proper spelling without altering code logic.
The commit corrects a duplicated word in a comment within the AMD DRM driver, changing 'the the' to 'the'. No functional code is altered.

The patch refactors the conv_uni_to_pc() function in tty/vt consolemap by loading the vc_uni_pagedir_loc pointer into a local variable with a NULL check, splitting a large conditional into smaller ones, and removing an unnecessary newline, solely to improve code readability.
Adds an entry to the MAINTAINERS file, listing the author as maintainer for the Allwinner A31 MIPI CSI-2 bridge media driver.
The commit adds a device‑specific quirk for Chicony Easycamera USB IDs in the uvcvideo driver, disabling or limiting the power line control because those cameras implement it incorrectly.
The commit corrects false detection of ODM combine mode changes for HDMI, removes unnecessary stream reprogramming, and enforces static ODM policy to stop intermittent black screens.

Removes the unit address from the panel endpoint node in the am335x device tree, because endpoint nodes must not have a unit address; this eliminates the need for a mandatory 'reg' property and fixes the DTS validation error.

The patch changes the hisilicon DRM driver to initialize on‑stack mode structures with drm_mode_init() instead of manual setup, ensuring the list head is properly cleared and avoiding uninitialized stack data.
The patch replaces direct uncore register accesses in i915 display code with intel_de_* accessor functions, centralising register handling.

Adds runtime checks in the amdgpu driver discovery code to ensure the number of VCN and SDMA instances reported by firmware does not exceed the size of the driver‑defined structures, preventing out‑of‑bounds handling.
The patch changes the s390 exception table handling to sort the amode31 extable earlier, ensuring the early program check handler can locate entries that were previously unsorted.

Removes the driver’s reset_resume callback for wireless Xbox 360 pads so that after suspend/resume the USB core rebinds the device, preventing a hung out‑URB that broke LED control and force feedback.
The patch changes fb_modesetting_disabled() to be a static‑inline function in its header, so each compilation unit gets its own copy, eliminating the multiple‑definition linker error reported.
The commit adds Clause‑45 MDIO PHY management support to the lan743x network driver, enabling communication with PHYs using the Clause‑45 MDIO protocol.
The commit adds a new stub header file (pfn.h) in tools/include, providing definitions required by test code.

The patch removes calls to acpi_video_set_dmi_backlight_type() in the toshiba_acpi driver to stop premature backlight unregistration that caused a race, and adds DMI quirks for two known transflective-display models.
The patch removes the driver’s call to the unsupported "dtim_assoc" IOVAR in brcmfmac, stopping repeated error messages after a Wi‑Fi roam because the firmware no longer provides TIM information.
Replace BUG_ON() with WARN_ON_ONCE() in signal handling so unexpected conditions are logged but execution continues, avoiding kernel panic and aiding debugging.

The patch removes three redundant variable initializations (bPacketMatchBSSID, bPacketToSelf, bPacketBeacon) from update_recvframe_phyinfo_88e in the r8188eu driver, because the variables are overwritten before any use.
The patch rewrites shmem_read_mapping_page_gfp() to call shmem_get_folio_gfp() directly, removing extra compound_head() calls and simplifying the internal shmem page‑retrieval path.
Adds validation for NTFS BOOT sectors_per_clusters shift value, ensuring it stays within allowed limits and returns -EINVAL otherwise, preventing invalid shift operations.
The patch fixes a null‑pointer dereference on RISC‑V when KASAN early init calls pfn_to_page before sparsemem structures are initialized, by removing that call.

Commit modifies dpaa2-eth to reuse the scatter‑gather table cache for normal packet processing, enlarges cached buffers to hold the maximum number of entries, and replaces per‑packet allocate/free with dpaa2_eth_sgt_get/recycle calls, reducing allocation overhead.
Updates the dt-bindings MAINTAINERS file to replace Krzysztof Kozlowski's email with his @kernel.org address.
Adds a new enum value "skip" to the qcom,gsi-loader DT property, allowing the device tree to indicate that GSI firmware is already loaded and should not be loaded by AP or modem.

Changes the Qualcomm SDM630 device‑tree to describe the TCSR mutex via MMIO instead of a syscon regmap, correcting the binding so the required ‘reg’ property is present and the syscon regex matches, thereby fixing DT schema validation errors.

Fixes a bug where returning from an interrupt to a soft‑masked (irqs‑disabled) context could lose a pending soft‑masked IRQ because the exit path for irqs‑enabled contexts was incorrectly used, clearing the wrong flag. The patch changes the exit handling to clear the proper flag and adds explanatory comments.

The patch sets the hotpluggable flag of all LoongArch I/O master CPUs to 0 and stops creating their /sys/.../online sysfs control files, because these CPUs cannot be hot‑plugged and the files mislead user‑space tools.
The patch cleans up the IA‑64 remove_siblinginfo() function by deleting the unused variable 'last' and the associated dead code, simplifying the implementation.

Updates the arm64 FP self‑test Makefile to build programs from TEST_GEN_PROGS_EXTENDED (compiled tests) instead of TEST_PROGS_EXTENDED (non‑compiled scripts), while keeping script tests in the latter.
The patch adds logic to fbcon_do_set_font() to undo font size changes when vc_resize() fails, preventing inconsistent console state after allocation failures reported by syzbot.
Adds a new 'power-domains' property description to the MediaTek video codec encoder device tree binding, documenting that the encoder may depend on a power domain.
The patch lowers the log severity of power and thermal envelope events on Gaudi2 devices from warning/error to informational, reflecting that they are not error conditions.
The commit updates the dt-bindings documentation for Hirschmann Hellcreek network devices to reference other schemas using absolute paths instead of relative ones.
The patch adds EXPORT_SYMBOL declarations for mt6358 driver functions that were missing, allowing other modules to link against them and eliminating undefined symbol errors during module build.
The commit reorders fields in the LTTPR UHBR link‑rate support structure of the AMD DRM driver to follow the field order defined by the DisplayPort 2.0 specification.

The patch updates the wcd9335 ASoC driver so the slimbus mux put operation checks whether the value actually changes; if unchanged it returns early, stopping the driver from reporting a change and generating spurious events.

The patch moves the acquisition of card->lock earlier in fw_core_handle_bus_reset so that accesses to card->local_node and card->bm_retries are protected, and removes redundant locking inside fw_destroy_nodes calls, adding a comment about required locking.

The patch moves the _set_policy function into the chip_ops structure of the rtw89 driver, allowing the RTL8852C chip to define additional coexistence policies (e.g., DBCC, multi‑role, TDMA). This restructures the driver to handle per‑chip policy differences.
Deletes an unnecessary assignment to the variable 'negative' in the ad2s1210 driver, which was never read before being overwritten, eliminating a clang dead store warning.

The patch changes the octeontx2 PF driver to forward AF replies to the VF without modifying them, preserving the error code set by AF. Previously PF altered the reply, causing the VF to miss error information.
The commit removes an obsolete flags check for CHIP_IP_DISCOVERY in the amdgpu DRM driver because IP‑based discovery is now fully supported, simplifying the code path.

The patch modifies the dw_hdmi driver to enable General Control Packets only when the sink reports Deep Color support, disabling automatic GCP for 24‑bit mode on sinks without Deep Color, to comply with HDMI 1.4b specification.
The patch modifies the ARM IRQ entry assembly to stop using register R9, which is reserved for the task pointer and must stay unchanged between IRQ entry and exit.
Implements VSC packet revision 4 in the AMD DRM driver, revising Start/End SDP data to follow the eDP 1.5 specification and enable PSR support.
The commit updates the tracing tools Makefile to add build, install, and clean rules for the rtla target, allowing rtla to be compiled and managed through the existing build system.
Adds a device‑tree compatible string for the PCA85073A RTC, enabling the existing PCF85063 driver to bind to this chip; verified on a custom i.MX6SX board.

The patch updates the Chrome EC Type‑C driver to set the parent pointer of a USB‑PD partner object via the registration wrapper, enabling the system to identify which Type‑C device a PD object belongs to.
Adds device‑tree nodes for an MMIO‑based MDIO multiplexer on the LS1043A‑QDS board, declares the FPGA as a simple‑mfd compatible device, and connects Ethernet interfaces to the new PHY nodes.
Adjusts the mt76 driver to set IEEE80211_VHT_CAP_TX_ANTENNA_PATTERN and RX_ANTENNA_PATTERN during stream initialization, ensuring antenna configuration is present for 6 GHz capabilities.
The patch adds a gfp_t parameter to convert_context() and its callers so that memory allocation uses GFP_ATOMIC inside the spinlock, eliminating the BUG caused by sleeping in atomic context.
Adds a platform shutdown callback for the WCN6750 Wi‑Fi device so it stops DMA before the SMMU driver is shut down, avoiding SMMU faults during system power‑off.

The patch updates the ocelot driver to handle bridge port flag configuration on the NPI port, redirecting the operation to the analyzer block index that maps to the CPU port, enabling the Felix DSA driver to control flooding to the CPU.
Adds support for the qcom,msm8974-mss-pil device tree binding by extending the existing MSM8916 schema with an extra mss-supply property, handled via a simple conditional.
Adds a defensive null check in dc_submit_i2c_oem to abort when the DDC pointer is NULL, preventing crashes from invalid calls.

Removes the i.MX8QM entry from the fsl-lpuart compatible enum in dt-bindings because it is backward compatible with i.MX8QXP, forcing nodes to list both compatible strings via the existing 'items' entry.

The patch reorders removal of an i915_gem_context from the global list until after its reference is dropped, preventing use‑after‑free of the list node that caused a general protection fault in i915_perf.
Adds a helper that allocates MSI‑X interrupt vectors for virtual queues and configuration interrupts in the vDPA ifcvf driver.
The patch removes an inappropriate snd_BUG_ON() check in snd_usbmidi_output_open() that triggered a kernel panic when a USB MIDI device presented an invalid endpoint, fixing the erroneous crash.

The patch modifies the Sony laptop keyboard backlight driver to skip probing for the 0x153 SNC handle, which lacks a dedicated probe address, preventing the probe from unintentionally turning the backlight off.

The patch limits 36‑bpp linebuffer usage to DCN display engines and forces DCE engines to use 30‑bpp, eliminating unwanted dithering on DCE‑11.2 hardware and restoring correct pixel passthrough for scientific applications.
The patch renames an inner variable named 'rate' in the mac80211 airtime code to avoid shadowing the outer 'rate' variable, eliminating confusion without altering functionality.
Replaces casts of literal addresses to (void *) in x86 boot code with absolute_pointer() macro, stopping GCC 11/12 false -Warray-bounds warnings.
Adds definitions for the LEDs and buttons of the Asus RTN-10U router in the MIPS BCM47XX platform driver, enabling the kernel to recognize and control these hardware elements.

The patch changes pinctrl actions to mark irq_chip structures as immutable, removes an unnecessary copy, sets IRQCHIP_IMMUTABLE flag, and adds helper calls to gpiolib to silence kernel warnings about mutable irq_chips.
Updates the imx8mp-phycore-som device tree: disables unused LDO4 and enables LDO5, which supplies VSEL for the NVCC_SD2 SD‑Card bus, correcting the regulator configuration.

The patch replaces generic clk_prepare_enable/disable calls with driver‑specific mchp_pit64b_suspend() and mchp_pit64b_resume() to correctly manage timer clocks during init and removal, aligning power‑management handling.
The patch unifies how underscores and dots are added to i915 microcode (UC) filenames by moving delimiter handling into the concatenation macro, removing explicit delimiters in the filename prefixes.
Adds a snd_card_free() call in the probe error path of the sonicvibes ALSA driver to correctly release resources before the card is registered, fixing a leak caused by prior devres cleanup.
Adds a new dmaengine driver for the Apple ADMAC audio DMA controller found in Apple Silicon SoCs, integrating it into the kernel.
The patch modifies the UDL DRM driver to pass a rectangle structure directly to udl_handle_damage(), removing intermediate handling and simplifying the code path.
Adds new self‑test cases for the BPF subsystem to verify correct handling of padding in btf_dump, using hand‑crafted and fuzz‑generated inputs.
Adds a call to unregister_candev() in the mcp251x_can_probe() error path to correctly clean up the CAN device when GPIO setup fails.
Adjusts indentation of a bullet list in thermal documentation to eliminate a Sphinx warning about missing blank line.
Adds over‑current detection for USB 1 on the Verdin i.MX8MP board by defining the USB_1_OC# pin (active‑low) in the device tree and removing its previous gpio_hog3 assignment.
Adds handling for the CMD_ERROR_EVENT command in the kvaser_usb driver, logging or safely ignoring an unexpected error event that should never be sent by the device.
Adds the _EL1 suffix to macro definitions for ID_AA64ISAR2_EL1 fields, aligning them with the convention of using full register names; no functional code changes.
Updates the CN10K egress ratelimit driver to use the new NIX_AF_TLXX_PIR/CIR register format, fixing burst exponent/mantissa handling and changing maxrate from u32 to u64 to match the stack.
The patch modifies the sfc driver by replacing BUG_ON checks with WARN_ON and adds code to recover from the condition, aiming to avoid kernel panic and address a checkpatch warning.

The patch changes the definition of the const array uid_strings in the Intel ASoC cirrus-common driver from a stack‑allocated variable to a static const object, moving it to read‑only data and reducing generated code size.
The patch defines a constant for the fixed value 0x6 and removes the never‑used UsbTxAggDescNum field from the hal_data_8188e struct in the r8188eu driver, cleaning up the data structure.
Adjusts uml_vector_default_bpf() to accept a const argument, aligning with the recent constification of MAC address structures.

The patch modifies the mt7915 driver testmode TX antenna configuration, replacing per‑band chainmask fields with a single antenna_mask for both band0 and band1, removing conversion logic when forming firmware commands and simplifying user configuration.

The patch clears the page->private pointer when a page is split or migrated, ensuring the PG_private flag and private pointer stay consistent. It adds zeroing after get_new_page() and after split_huge_page() to fix cases where page->private was left uninitialized.
Corrects a spelling mistake in a comment within the ASoC AMD ACP driver.
Adds updated register and field definitions for the Mediatek Ethernet PCS based on recent investigation, reflecting differences from the Lynx PCS.

The patch updates the fbdev hot‑unplug workaround for framebuffers lacking a device. It adds a kernel warning and rewrites the surrounding comment, noting that the workaround is obsolete now that each OF framebuffer has a platform device.
The commit changes F2FS to treat a zoned block device as having one uniform zone capacity, removing per‑zone capacity handling to simplify the filesystem implementation.
The commit updates all source files to replace the GPLv2 boilerplate with the SPDX identifier 'GPL-2.0-only', standardizing license declarations across the tree.
The patch deletes the now‑unused declaration of sni_cpu_time_init() after earlier changes removed all its calls, cleaning up dead code in the MIPS time‑keeping subsystem.

The patch modifies the AMD DRM display driver to increase the command buffer (compbuf) size before the driver updates GPU clocks. Previously the compbuf size was set after clock updates, which could cause P‑State hangs. By programming the larger compbuf earlier, the hang is avoided.
Adds a device‑tree node for the Mediatek MT6795 pinctrl controller, declaring its presence while leaving pin configuration to machine‑specific DTs.
The commit corrects various misspelled words in the ath10k Wi‑Fi driver, as reported by the codespell tool, without altering functionality.
Removes a redundant resource check in the USB c67x00 driver’s remove function because the probe already validated the resource.
Updates KVM x86 documentation for MSR filtering, clarifying terminology, fixing an off‑by‑one description error, and removing redundant text.

The patch updates memory‑management code to call folio_swap_flags directly instead of converting a folio to a page and using page_swap_flags. The sole caller already has a folio, so the conversion is moved down, simplifying the call chain.
The patch modifies the error string emitted by the mlx5e driver when changing LRO state, replacing the old specific wording with a newer, more generic name.
Adds support for nested VMLOAD/VMSAVE instructions in KVM on x86 AMD SVM, enabling proper nested virtualization handling and verified by multi-level Linux guest testing.
Stops overwriting the sdw_msg buffer on write commands, treating it as const, to prevent caller data corruption in the SoundWire Cadence driver.
The patch modifies the intel_soc_pmic_bxtwc driver to reuse a temporary struct device variable more widely, simplifying the code and improving readability.
The patch moves local variables of dml32_CalculateSwathAndDETConfiguration into a temporary structure, reducing the function's stack frame in the AMD DRM display driver.
Refactors the Chinese admin-guide documentation index, reformatting the ToDo list in the generated HTML for a cleaner appearance.
The patch moves the TSC ratio definitions used by the SVM KVM implementation into the svm.h header, matching the SVM specification and improving code organization.
Adds documentation for the Renesas RZ/G2UL USB2 PHY bindings, noting it matches the RZ/G2L PHY and can use the existing compatible string as fallback.

The commit refactors the ltc2983 temperature driver to obtain configuration values via a generic device‑property interface, allocating a single buffer for all values instead of per‑value reads, making the driver independent of OF and usable on other platforms.
The commit updates the STM32 device tree to include an alternate pin multiplexing configuration for the DCMI pins, required for AV96 board support.
The commit reverts a previous sbitmap fix because it introduced CPU stalls and possible infinite loops; restoring the original code stops the regression.
The commit deletes the q->qid member from the mt76 driver because it is no longer referenced, cleaning up dead code.

The patch saves the device's base register before freeing the MMC host and uses that saved value instead of dereferencing the freed host pointer in moxart_remove(), eliminating a reported use‑after‑free.
The patch updates mac80211 MLME code to set the sta.mlo flag when a station uses Multi‑Link Operation, fixing an omission introduced by prior rebasing.
Adds minimal register set (regset) definitions for the m68k architecture, enabling core‑dump support of the elf_fdpic loader; code is conditional and provides only the required infrastructure.
The commit updates the imx319 I2C camera driver to mark the flip controls with V4L2_CTRL_FLAG_MODIFY_LAYOUT, informing V4L2 that the image layout (Bayer order) changes when flips are applied.
The commit changes the function process_msg_close in the rnbd-srv driver to return void instead of int, because it always returned 0, removing an unnecessary return value.
Adds support for the SBI v0.3 System Reset (SRST) extension in the RISC‑V KVM hypervisor, enabling guest power‑off and reboot via the standard SBI interface.
Adds 16-byte NOP padding before every function on x86, aligning functions to 16 bytes and preparing the kernel for software call‑stack tracking and kCFI/FineIBT, with no observed performance impact.
The commit renames the clock identifier video_pll1 to video_pll in the i.MX driver to match the reference manual, keeping old constants for compatibility, with no functional changes.

The patch updates i9xx_update_wm() in the i915 DRM driver to call the existing single_enabled_crtc() helper instead of a custom ad‑hoc check, and removes an unused 'enabled' variable, aligning the code with other legacy WM functions.

Adds a guard in the AMD DRM driver to verify that a PSR-enabled panel has already entered PSR before attempting to enter MALL state, and prevents overwriting link settings when programming a phantom stream sharing the same link.
Changes audit_init_parent to take a const char * path, improving const‑correctness of the function signature.
Adds support for mono audio streams in the tas2770 ASoC driver by enabling downmix and channel switching, allowing the right channel range to be used for mono playback.
The patch updates the STM32 VREFBUF regulator driver to replace pm_runtime_get_sync calls with pm_runtime_resume_and_get, simplifying runtime‑PM handling.

The patch changes the Intel raw NAND driver to read the chip‑select line from the flash device's own device‑tree node (a child of the NAND controller) instead of the controller node, fixing the source of the CS value.
The commit replaces the existing shouty macros that compute XFS inode fork sizes with static inline helper functions, adding type checking and improving code safety and readability.

The patch corrects hci_read_buffer_size_sync to stop using the LE‑only opcode HCI_OP_LE_READ_BUFFER_SIZE_V2 and instead use the appropriate generic read‑buffer‑size path, fixing incorrect handling of buffer size queries for non‑LE Bluetooth devices.
Changes the r888eu driver to allocate the efuse buffer with kmalloc and free it on exit, replacing a fixed 512‑byte stack array and dropping the __aligned(4) qualifier.
The commit marks several functions in dcn32_hubbub.c as static because they are only used within that file, removing external linkage and eliminating compiler warnings about missing prototypes.
The commit revises the PTP OCP driver to compute sysfs attribute groups before registration and uses sysfs_create_groups, avoiding sysfs_remove_group on unregistered groups that caused a crash.
The patch deletes the declaration of the function intel_gt_create_kobj() from drm/i915/gt because it is not referenced anywhere, cleaning up dead code.

The patch edits the max9759 driver Kconfig to drop an unconditional 'select GPIOLIB' because GPIO support is optional, preventing forced inclusion of the gpiolib subsystem and eliminating build‑time warnings in random configurations.
Introduces folio_batch_move_lru() and rewrites LRU handling in swap from pagevecs to folio_batches, merging existing pagevec helper logic into new folio_batch functions.

The patch deletes an unnecessary f2fs_lock_op call in f2fs_new_inode because f2fs_alloc_nid() does not need to block checkpoint and __f2fs_build_free_nids() is already protected by nat_tree_lock, simplifying the code.
Adds an is_subset helper to the perf cpumap code that returns true when the second cpumap is a subset of the first, extending the cpumap API.
The patch updates the lynxpoint pinctrl driver to explicitly include required header files that were previously missing and orders the include list alphabetically.

The patch removes the functions tcf_connmark_walker() and tcf_connmark_search() from the act_connmark scheduler because they duplicate the behavior of a generic walk/search helper, simplifying the codebase.
The patch corrects the nouveau driver for TU102 GPUs so that the sw_bundle64_init command includes the high 32 bits of the value, which were previously omitted.
Updates the rkvdec driver to call the new vb2_find_buffer helper, retrieving a vb2_buffer by its timestamp instead of the previous lookup method.
Adds new unit tests for the MCTP subsystem to verify key/tag lookup behavior on routed packets by inserting specific entries and checking match/mismatch outcomes.
Adds a manual snd_card_free() call in the cs46xx driver’s probe error path to correctly release resources before the card is registered, fixing a leak caused by devres cleanup ordering.
The patch updates the mxsfb DRM driver to use the dev_err_probe() helper instead of hand‑written error logging, adding a helpful entry in /sys/kernel/debug/devices_deferred.
The patch changes bootmem code to store free page information in page->index instead of page->freelist, using the same bits but an integer field to eliminate pointer casts.
The patch updates the sdw-mockup driver to use the new snd_sdw_params_to_config helper for converting hw_params to SoundWire configuration, replacing existing conversion code.

The patch corrects refcount handling in configfs_make_dirent() for error paths of configfs_create_dir(), adding a configfs_put() call to avoid leaked sd and fragment objects, thus fixing a memory leak reported by kmemleak.

The patch changes the error codes returned by xdp_do_redirect() for AF_XDP zero‑copy redirects, distinguishing allocation failures (ENOMEM) from Rx buffer full (ENOBUFS) instead of using ENOSPC for both.
The patch changes NVMe PCI reset handling: on reset failure it no longer unbinds the driver but simply shuts down the controller, leaving it in a dead state.
Adds schema constraints to device‑tree OPP binding child nodes, setting unevaluatedProperties or additionalProperties to false so only documented properties are allowed.

The patch corrects a memory leak in the io_uring file registration path: when __io_sqe_files_scm() finds no files, it frees resources but fails to release the associated uid reference, leading to leaked memory. The commit adds the missing uid put.
Adds Kconfig selections for generic CBC and AES as fallbacks for the __cbc-aes-neonbs algorithm on ARM, ensuring the algorithm can register during boot.

Adds a runtime check in the ASoC core that detects when drivers use the generic wrapping method to set the driver field in snd_ctl_card_info and prints an error, urging proper initialization to avoid truncation and name clashes.
Adds a new ASoC board configuration (adl_rt5682) for Intel platforms that lack a speaker amplifier, wiring the alc5682 headset codec to SSP0 per Intel BT offload design.
The patch removes the gfp_flags argument from null_alloc_page(), which was always passed as GFP_NOIO by null_insert_page(), and updates callers to use the default behavior, simplifying the API.
Adds a minimal sysfs stub for DAMON, creating a hierarchy of sysfs directories and files to control virtual address space monitoring, moving away from the debugfs interface.
Adds a NET dependency to INTEL_HFI_THERMAL in Kconfig so that THERMAL_NETLINK's NET requirement is satisfied, removing a Kconfig warning and numerous build errors.
Corrects swapped bitmask values in RX_DMA_GET_SPORT and RX_DMA_GET_SPORT_V2 macros of the MediaTek Ethernet driver, ensuring proper source‑port extraction.

The patch corrects the prefetch calculation loop in the AMD DCN3.2 display driver by resetting local variables each iteration, ensuring the loop exits correctly instead of consuming the entire vstartup after a failure.

The patch fixes a race condition in the roccat HID driver where reports are freed without synchronization, leading to a use‑after‑free during roccat_read(). It adds proper locking or safe handling to prevent the kfree() from occurring while copy_to_user() accesses the buffer.
The commit removes the CONFIG_DRM_AMD_DC_DCN Kconfig option from the amdgpu_dm directory because it is redundant and was only used to bypass compilation errors, making the DC code truly OS‑agnostic.
The patch modifies mac80211 code so that when the DTIM period is set it is stored in link->conf->dtim_period and not cleared afterwards, while still using beacon data when present.
The patch adds the list_for_each_table_entry macro to the proc sysctl code, replacing manual traversal of ctl_table with a macro to make the loop cleaner and more readable.

The patch changes io_uring’s multishot accept handling so that when the completion‑queue entry (CQE) ring overflows, the pending multishot accept request is dropped, similar to the existing multishot poll behavior.
Adds a call to mv88e6xxx_get_caps() during port setup so CPU/DSA ports obtain correct MAC capabilities, fixing the default 10 Mbps speed caused by missing capabilities after earlier changes.
The commit updates ath10k driver source to silence new checkpatch warnings by replacing strlcpy with strscpy and fixing an unnecessary integer promotion in a printf format string.
Updates the it66121 device‑tree binding header to document and enable audio support for the ITE HDMI bridge.

Adds a check in the io_uring networking path so that zerocopy sendmsg operations are rejected with an error when the underlying socket does not support zerocopy, mirroring earlier handling for zerocopy send.
Adds ethtool --identify support to the nfp driver, enabling the NIC firmware to blink the panel LED when the command is invoked.
Adds device‑tree binding definitions for the Himax hx83112b touchscreen, providing the necessary documentation files so the kernel can describe and support this hardware.
Adds a regulator node and enables the PCIe 2 controller and its combphy in the quartz64-b device tree for Rockchip arm64 platforms, extending hardware support.

The patch separates the responsibilities of nvme_kill_queues: it renames the part that marks all namespace gendisks dead to nvme_mark_namespaces_dead and moves the unquiescing of I/O queues out to the callers, reflecting that the two actions are now independent.
The patch removes an unnecessary check for Correctable Error (CE) status when querying RAS Uncorrectable Error (UE) address in the amdgpu DRM driver, simplifying the code path.

The commit resolves Sparse static analysis warnings in PowerPC time code by adding missing declarations, including proper headers, removing duplicate definitions, and reordering definitions to follow includes.
The commit updates the Merrifield GPIO driver to replace duplicated enable/disable code with a call to the existing str_enable_disable() helper, improving code reuse.
Adds a conditional test for xeCJK.sty in the kerneldoc preamble, loading it only if the file exists, to avoid xelatex errors on systems where texlive-xecjk is not installed.
The patch updates NFS code to use struct sockaddr_storage in memcpy calls, matching the actual union size and eliminating false positive fortify warnings about field‑spanning writes.
The patch updates Btrfs code to use the OFFSET_MAX macro instead of INT_LIMIT(loff_t), improving readability by using a self‑describing constant for the maximum file offset.
The patch removes the obsolete of_gpio.h header from the zevio GPIO driver and updates the code to use newer of_* APIs and structures, cleaning up the driver.

The patch modifies the AMD KFD driver to correct how compute unit (CU) masks are generated on GFX10+ GPUs that use work‑group processors (WGP). It forces the mask to be pairwise contiguous and distributes CUs round‑robin across shader engines, assuming WGP mode.
The commit updates the max14656 power supply driver to replace a custom delayed‑work implementation with the kernel helper devm_delayed_work_autocancel(), reducing code size.
Adds a hardware capability flag (hwcap) for ARM64 MTE asymmetric mode (FEAT_MTE3) so user‑space can detect its support via the standard hwcap mechanism.
The patch extracts combo PHY register definitions from the generic i915 register header into a dedicated header, limiting their inclusion to the few files and platforms that actually need them.
The patch modifies the Palmas MFD driver to obtain its match data directly via device_get_match_data(), removing custom handling and simplifying the code.
The commit updates the ptp_pch driver to use the generic ioread64_hi_lo() and iowrite64_hi_lo() helpers for 64‑bit I/O, replacing any custom handling.
The patch deletes the sx8 block driver files, as the hardware is obsolete and the driver has been unmaintained since 2005, cleaning up the kernel source tree.
The commit updates the Qualcomm USB VBUS regulator DT binding by renaming the generic node name from "dcdc" to "usb-vbus-regulator" and adjusts the example accordingly.
Adds the UNTRAIN_RET speculation‑mitigation macro to the Xen entry path on x86, ensuring the entry code executes the barrier.
Removes the obsolete <linux/gpio.h> header from the i2c ccs driver, keeping only the needed <linux/gpio/consumer.h> include.

The patch updates the kbuild header‑check test to stop including include/linux/cyclades.h, because that header now emits a warning indicating it should never be used. The file is removed from the list of headers the test scans.

Adds ability to override the DMA mapping device in the mt76 driver so that the WED driver can use non‑coherent DMA while the PCI device may be configured for coherent DMA; the WED driver will adjust the PCI HIF coherent I/O setting on attach.
The patch renames btrfs_insert_file_extent() to btrfs_insert_hole_extent() because the function only inserts hole extents, and removes parameters that are no longer used, improving code clarity.

Fixes a memory leak in the OrangeFS kernel module by ensuring the debug_help_string buffer allocated in orangefs_prepare_debugfs_help_string() is freed when the module is removed or when the string is changed.
Updates the Qualcomm ADSP remoteproc device tree binding to simplify interrupt constraints, reflecting that variants only differ by an optional last interrupt.
The patch raises the GT reset‑failure timeout from 5 s to 60 s in the i915 driver, preventing premature device wedge and data loss when a reset takes longer, as reported in issue 6448.
Adds handling for PTP timestamp interrupts in the sparx5 network driver, allowing the driver to read timestamps from the FIFO when a 2‑step timestamping event occurs.
Adds a new 'requires_cpu' flag in perf's event selection code to distinguish uncore events that need a specific CPU from system-wide events, correcting the semantics of the existing system_wide flag.
Adds kernel documentation strings for core domain fields in the Tegra PMC driver, enabling kerneldoc generation; no functional code change.
The patch adds a null‑pointer check after calling platform_get_resource() in the mt6397 RTC driver to avoid dereferencing a NULL pointer.

The patch renames the existing filter group identifiers in the mlx5 bridge driver from generic 'fg' to 'vlan_filter' in functions, variables and definitions, to distinguish them from a forthcoming QinQ filter group, improving code readability.
Removes the now‑unused declaration of arch_kprobe_override_function() from x86/kprobes after a prior commit eliminated all its calls, cleaning up dead code.

The patch wraps the -mno-branch-likely compiler flag with cc-option for MIPS Loongson targets, preventing clang warnings from becoming errors, and moves the flag check into Kconfig to run at configuration time.

The patch replaces calls to of_irq_get_byname with the generic fwnode_irq_get_byname in platform code, allowing both OF and ACPI described devices to obtain named interrupts via the fwnode abstraction.
Adds a new helper function hda_codec_device_remove() in the Intel SOF ASoC driver to separate removal handling between the controller and codec, improving code organization.
Adds the mmhub v3_0_1 register header files to the amdgpu driver to support the newer hardware version, noting differences from the previous v3_0_0 headers.
Replaces sprintf with snprintf in ptp_ocp_verify() to make the code easier to review and potentially safer.
The patch replaces devres_alloc()/devres_add() with devm_add_action_or_reset() in devm_clk_hw_register_clkdev(), simplifying the implementation without altering behavior.
Adds a runtime validation of the user‑provided CQ counter offset in the habanalabs driver for the wait_for_interrupt and register_for_timestamp APIs.

The patch updates a printf format string in the Gaudi driver: the variable div_sel is a u32 but was printed with %d. The format specifier is changed to match the unsigned 32‑bit type, correcting the output and avoiding undefined behavior.

Adds support for additional TC flower filter keys in the Microchip Sparx5 driver’s IS2 VCAP, enabling matching on IPv4/IPv6 addresses, fragments, ports, protocols, VLAN tags, TCP flags, and IP TOS, plus a 128‑bit keyfield for IPv6.
Adds IRQ handling support for Meson S4 SoCs by defining the expanded set of GPIO IRQ lines and their mapping.
Adds a new cpufeatures flag for AMD PerfMonV2 by parsing CPUID leaf 0x80000022, exposing the capability and PMC count registers so the kernel can use the new performance monitoring hardware.
Adds code to free the rwi structure when the last reset entry succeeds, eliminating a 32‑byte memory leak introduced by a prior commit.

The patch casts the return value of __fls to unsigned long in the Intel AVS ASoC driver so that the %ld format specifier matches the type on arc, m68k and sparc, eliminating a build‑time warning and allowing the kernel to compile on those architectures.
The commit renames ice_sriov.c and its header to ice_vf_mbx.c to reflect that the file contains generic VF mailbox code, preparing for future Scalable IOV support.

The patch modifies f2fs_inode_info by splitting the existing cp_task field into cp_task (used for FS_CP_DATA_IO accounting) and wb_task (used to avoid deadlocks). This corrects a regression where, with the data_flush mount option, background data‑flush I/O was incorrectly counted as checkpoint I/O.

Adds a guard in ieee80211_tx_control_port() to skip __ieee80211_select_queue() when the hardware reports fewer than four queues, fixing a regression that caused invalid queue IDs and association failures on rt2500-pci and similar drivers.
The commit adds driver support for the Multi‑Gigabit Ethernet (MGBE/XPCS) hardware present in NVIDIA Tegra234 SoCs within the stmmac network driver.
Adds missing string entries for two iavf driver init states so debug prints show correct state names instead of UNKNOWN_STATE.
The commit modifies perf inject to copy the kcore_dir directory from the input perf.data into the output file, preserving kallsyms and related files for later analysis.
Updates the sun4i_can device‑tree binding to include the common CAN controller binding defined in can-controller.yaml, improving the DT binding documentation.
The commit relocates the Renesas PRR device tree binding file from the soc directory to a new hwinfo directory, grouping chip ID and SoC information under hwinfo for better organization.
The patch removes an explicit cast to u8 when comparing two u8 fields (card_8192_version and IC_Cut) against a macro already defined as u8, simplifying the driver code.
The patch deletes an unnecessary #include of linux/msi.h from the iommu/of source file because the file does not use any symbols from that header.

The commit adds a new algorithm for setting BCH ECC geometry when NAND devices have OOB size >1KB, ensuring the bad‑block mark stays within data chunks, and falls back to a separate ECC for metadata if needed.

The patch wraps the Energy Model‑specific functions cppc_get_cpu_cost and cppc_get_cpu_power in #ifdef CONFIG_ENERGY_MODEL guards, so they are only compiled when the energy model is enabled. This removes the unused‑function warnings that cause build failures and avoids executing unnecessary code when the feature is disabled.

Updates octeontx2-af driver source files to initialize previously uninitialized variables and add checks, removing smatch static analysis warnings about uninitialized symbols and possible ERR_PTR dereferences.

The commit edits the Exynos850 device‑tree to drop wake‑up interrupt entries that were incorrectly placed in the main device node, keeping only the proper interrupt definition in the pin‑controller node.
The patch adds interrupt configuration and handling code for the Micrel ksz9477 PHY driver, aligning it with other Micrel PHYs that already support interrupts.

Adds support for the t6000 DART IOMMU page table entry format used in Apple M1 Pro/Max/Ultra SoCs, handling 42‑bit physical addresses and mandatory sub‑page protection by configuring it to allow full‑page access.
The patch modifies scripts/checkpatch.pl to stop flagging macros that contain a 'case' statement as errors, recognizing that such macros are used in drivers.

The patch replaces a manual size calculation in pwc_decompress() with the struct_size() helper, removing a flexible‑struct warning and preventing integer‑overflow scenarios that could lead to heap overflows.
The patch replaces calls to nodes_weight() with nodes_empty() in arch/x86 code where only a check for any set bit is needed, because nodes_empty() can stop early and is more efficient.
Adds a dma-channel-mask property to the Tegra GPCDMA device‑tree node and updates the interrupts list to include all 32 channels, correcting the previous driver limitation to 31 channels.

The patch adds checks that, when a KVM x86 vendor module loads, use the corrected KVM_X86_OP annotations to detect and emit warnings if any function pointers in the kvm_x86_ops structure are NULL, preventing possible NULL‑pointer dereferences.

The patch modifies KVM self‑tests by removing the generic vm_xsave_req_perm call, moving it into the amx_test, and adding a parameter to customize which xsave bit is requested, allowing other tests to use it differently.

The patch updates the VC4 HDMI driver to correctly detect the hdmi_enable_4kp60 configuration flag by replacing the old clk_round_rate() check with clk_get_max_rate(), which now returns the true maximum clock rate after a recent clock subsystem change.

The patch modifies devm_hwmon_device_register_with_info() so that its 'chip' argument must be supplied, preventing drivers from merely renaming calls to the old hwmon_device_register() without providing proper chip information.
The commit updates the lm90 hardware monitoring driver to replace a left‑shift expression with the BIT macro, improving code readability without altering behavior.
Adds a PowerPC64‑specific module loader check that validates the ELF ABI version of a module before loading, overriding the generic ELF check.

The patch switches simple‑KMS helper functions in the simpledrm driver to the standard DRM atomic helpers, removes empty CRTC enable/disable helpers, and always calls drm_atomic_helper_check_plane_state(). No runtime behavior changes, only internal refactoring for better architecture and code reuse.

Commit replaces manual cancel_delayed_work_sync() in the sbs‑charger driver’s remove() path with devm_delayed_work_autocancel(), which automatically handles cancellation only when the delayed work was initialized, and removes the now‑redundant remove() function.
Adds a call to devlink_port_type_clear() in the mlx4 driver cleanup when devlink_port_type_set() was previously used, ensuring the port type state is properly cleared.
Adds a JPEG decode worker interface in the Media driver to allow three hardware decoders to run in parallel on the MT8195 SoC.

The patch updates the cdce925 clock driver to use the new simple I2C probe mechanism. It replaces the old probe that required an id argument with i2c_match_id to obtain driver data, allowing the driver to be probed via probe_new.
The patch replaces a hand‑written delayed‑work implementation in the da9063 driver with the kernel helper devm_delayed_work_autocancel(), shortening the code and using device‑managed resources.

Moves the handling of the keep_towrite flag from ext4_writepage() to ext4_bio_write_page() so that pages with unwritable buffers retain the TOWRITE tag, preventing WB_SYNC_ALL from skipping them and causing data loss, especially during transaction commit.
The commit moves the lookup of a devlink snapshot ID to the caller, simplifying devlink_nl_region_read_snapshot_fill, removing an unused parameter, and enabling early exit on invalid IDs.
The commit raises the deprecation delay for SELinux's checkreqprot and runtime‑disable knobs from 5 s to 15 s, making the warning more visible to users still using these deprecated options.
Adds support for up to three CAN-FD channels in the gs_usb driver for STM32G3 devices, increasing the driver’s channel limit from the previous value.
The patch deletes the variable 'found_devs' from the qla2xxx SCSI driver because it is only incremented and never used elsewhere, eliminating dead code.
The patch deletes VPRINTK debug prints in libata and removes the ata_scsi_dump_cdb() helper because tracepoints already provide the same information, cleaning up redundant code.
The commit corrects a kernel-doc comment in drivers/hv/vmbus_drv.c so the documented prototype matches the actual __vmbus_child_driver_register function, eliminating a build warning.

The patch relaxes the requirement to hold the iSCSI back_lock when calling iscsi_get_task, adding logic to detect the final put before freeing the task, aiming to reduce lock contention and improve performance.

The patch rewrites DRM EDID logging to use device‑specific macros (drm_kms_dbg, drm_err), adds a standardized connector identifier format [CONNECTOR:%d:%s], passes connector structures where needed, and condenses tile debug output to a single line, improving consistency and readability.

The commit refactors PCI power management by extracting the post‑delay portion of pci_power_up() into a new helper pci_set_full_power_state(), called only where needed, eliminating redundant work for one caller.

The patch updates the i915 driver to drop Intel Ice Lake (ICL) specific Thunderbolt AUX power well definitions and adopt the generic TBT1‑4 names from the hardware specification, cleaning up power domain handling.
The patch deletes the remaining IDE driver documentation files that were left after the IDE driver removal, consolidating the changes with a prior documentation cleanup commit.

The patch modifies amdgpu_display_framebuffer_init to skip tiling‑flag validation when virtual display (vkms) is enabled, because vkms lacks FB modifiers, thereby removing a warning on GFX9+ hardware.
Adds a hypervisor check to skip the WBINVD cache‑flush in ACPI sleep handling, because inside VMs it is unnecessary and on TDX guests triggers a #VE exception.
The patch tightens tcp_read_sock() by detecting a bad return from recv_actor(), emitting a one‑time warning and forcing progress to avoid an infinite loop.
Changes rhashtable synchronization from bh‑safe to irq‑safe, updating lock/unlock helpers to return flags and accept them directly, allowing the hash table to be used in interrupt context.
Adds an explicit length check before memset in vtpm_proxy_fops_read to silence a GCC -Warray-bounds warning and make the code safe if proxy_dev->req_len changes.

The commit updates the yas530 IIO driver to use DEFINE_RUNTIME_DEV_PM_OPS() and pm_ptr() macros, enabling the compiler to drop the dev_pm_ops structure and related functions when CONFIG_PM is disabled, removing the need for __maybe_unused annotations.
The commit updates RTC driver source files to include <linux/kstrtox.h> instead of <linux/kernel.h> because the kstrto* conversion functions were relocated to the new header.

The commit adds calls to sdma_v5_2_enable(false) during hw_fini and re‑enables it after resume when running under SRIOV, ensuring the shared SDMA engine is correctly reset and preventing premature use during resume.
The patch adds a generic timeout function interface to the MediaTek JPEG decoder driver, enabling handling of hardware timeouts.

Adds capability for AMD DRM driver to enter low‑power zstate during the extra vertical blank period created by FreeSync video mode, calculating available time and adjusting registers, with restore on exit.
The commit deletes the ipa_fw_mem reserved memory node from the trogdor device tree overlay, eliminating a memory region overlap that caused a boot-time error on trogdor boards.

The patch updates Btrfs's merge_state function to replace direct rb_next/rb_prev traversal of the extent I/O tree with the next_state/prev_state helper functions, simplifying and cleaning up the code.

The commit updates the function pointer prototype for hqd_destroy() so its third parameter type matches the actual implementations (enum kfd_preempt_type), eliminating a kernel CFI type mismatch that caused a runtime failure on certain GPUs.

The commit updates the arm64 device tree for the Meson SM1 Odroid board, correcting the GPIO pin and setting it to open‑drain for the tf‑io regulator, which eliminates the boot loop that occurs after a reboot.

The patch consolidates duplicated fsnotify logic for handling events on child inodes when the parent inode has a mark without FS_EVENT_ON_CHILD. It moves this handling into the mark type iterator preparation, excluding the parent mark type and correcting mask clearing and event ignoring issues.

Adds support for multiple BAR configurations (0, 2, 4) in NTB endpoint function, storing BAR numbers in ntb_epf_data so different VID/PID can select appropriate mapping, increasing flexibility of memory BAR mapping.
Updates the STM32 pinctrl device‑tree binding: renames the property from 'reset' to the correct 'resets' and adds 'additionalProperties: false' to the schema.
Adds propagation of timestamping flags in the IPv6 ping (ping6) implementation so that requested packet timestamps are actually delivered.
Adds a compatible entry for the Microchip Icicle reference design in the RISC‑V device‑tree bindings, documenting the FPGA fabric version it targets.

Adds proper error handling in rio_register_mport(): on device_register() failure it releases the device reference with put_device() so the name allocated by dev_set_name() is freed, and removes the port from rio_mports list.

The patch separates kernel‑only capability flags from the user‑visible ib_device::device_cap_flags, introduces a new kernel_cap_flags bitmap, adds explanatory comments, and drops unused flags, clarifying the API boundary.

The patch modifies ath9k_hw_resettxqueue to silence a GCC‑12 array‑bounds warning about accessing txq[32] on a 10‑element array, likely via a cast, pragma, or index adjustment, without changing runtime behavior.

The patch updates KVM's CPUID handling for x86 so that when the base XFD feature flag is not reported, the per‑state‑component XFD bits (sub‑function i of CPUID 0Dh) are cleared, ensuring KVM's CPUID output respects the Intel XFD dependency.
Adds explicit linux/highmem.h and linux/swap.h includes where needed, enabling removal of the indirect linux/i2c.h include from i915_drv.h and cleaning up header dependencies.

Adds a boolean flag in the mlx5 driver to remember whether the vport ACL namespace has been created, so it is not freed and recreated on each e-switch mode change; it is only freed on driver unload or bare‑metal mode.
Adds logic to the bq25892 driver to read the usb_type property from an external charger‑detecting power‑supply device and set the IINLIM register accordingly.
The patch replaces all occurrences of SERIAL_XMIT_SIZE with UART_XMIT_SIZE in the serial subsystem, removing the duplicate macro and standardizing on UART_XMIT_SIZE.

Refactors the KVM self‑test xapic_ipi_test to stop using *_VCPU_ID macros, switching vm_create_with_one_vcpu to vm_create_with_vcpus() and passing struct kvm_vcpu pointers instead of numeric IDs, simplifying the test code.

The patch extracts the nearly identical NAT execution code from OVS and TC, places it in a new netfilter file nf_nat_ovs.c, and exports nf_ct_nat() for shared use, while keeping OVS/TC‑specific checks and flag updates. It also standardizes protocol extraction via skb_protocol().
The patch removes direct calls to the internal da7219_aad_jack_det() function in the Rockchip ASoC driver and replaces them with the generic component->set_jack() API.
Deletes several unused AVIC function prototypes from kvm_x86_ops after they were removed during a switch to optional static calls, with no impact on kernel behavior.

The patch updates the self‑test script test_lirc_mode2.sh to return a non‑zero exit status when the user test fails and to correctly handle the LIRCDEV check by quoting the variable, ensuring proper skip behavior under bash -n.
The patch deletes the obsolete enum odm_bw from the r8188eu driver, retaining the equivalent ht_channel_width enum, thus removing redundancy.

The commit updates the perf test suite for the "perf stat CSV output linter" (test 83) to handle the different CSV field count on s390 by replacing a Python comma‑counting script with a Bash function, making the test pass on that architecture.
Adds an explicit gpiolib header include to the midas_wm811 ASoC driver, removing reliance on indirect inclusion and preventing compilation errors in some kernel configurations.
The commit fixes the AD4130 driver sysfs documentation formatting by converting the mode list into a bullet list with blank lines, eliminating Sphinx indentation warnings.
The commit adds support for the RPC-IF module clock on the Renesas R8A779G0 SoC and corrects a table alignment issue in the RPCSRC internal clock definition.
The patch reallocates the SCSI device's budget_map after slave_configure() updates the queue depth, ensuring the map size matches the actual hardware limits and avoids unnecessary memory allocation.
Removes a register write in GV100 shader exception initialization to align the driver with the reference RM behavior.

The commit adds an extensible rseq ABI. It makes the kernel expose the supported rseq feature size and required alignment to user-space via ELF auxiliary vectors, allowing registration with the original 32‑byte struct or larger structs.
The patch updates the sun8i-ss crypto driver to replace pm_runtime_get_sync calls with pm_runtime_resume_and_get, using a more suitable runtime‑PM API and simplifying the code.
Updates two vt6655 driver macros, renaming the variable wData to reg_value to comply with kernel naming conventions and satisfy checkpatch.pl.
The patch refactors the hisi_sas SCSI driver by having slave_configure_v3_hw() call the existing hisi_sas_slave_configure() function, eliminating duplicated code.
Renames parameters of amdgpu_ring_init in both header and source so that the declaration and definition use identical names (ring_size → max_dw, prio → hw_prio).

The patch modifies the Bluetooth driver suspend routine to always set the event mask after successful disconnects, ensuring the mask is applied even when wakeup is disabled, preventing premature wakeups.

Adds a 1 MiB upper bound and overflow‑safe calculations for the temporary OSS PCM conversion buffer, preventing vmalloc() from exceeding INT_MAX and triggering WARN_ON, addressing a syzbot‑reported overflow.
Adds support for the Quectel EM05‑G USB modem in the option driver, handling its two USB configurations (RMNET and MBIM) and the associated interfaces.
Adds a new power‑supply driver for the uPI uG3105 battery monitor, integrating it into the kernel's power subsystem for x86/ACPI platforms.
The patch changes hugetlb_cgroup_from_page() to operate on folios, updates __remove_hugetlb_page() accordingly, and deletes the unused hugetlb_cgroup_from_page_resv() helper.
The patch raises the hard‑reset delay in the Gaudi2 driver from 500 ms to 2 s so that firmware and preboot finish before registers are accessed, preventing premature register reads.

The patch modifies the i2c remove callback of the jsa1212 light driver to return 0 instead of an error, because the driver already reports errors in its power_off routine. This eliminates a duplicate error message from the i2c core and prepares the driver for future callbacks that return void.

The patch moves the fixed‑file install/remove helpers into the filetable subsystem and changes their API to accept a context (ctx) instead of an io_kiocb, reflecting that the operation is not tied to a specific request.
Adds an IOCTL interface to the Xilinx firmware driver so users can enable/disable runtime features and query or set their configuration, capabilities that did not exist before.
Adds a dt-binding documentation entry for the ti,set-io-isolation property of the wkup_m3_ipc node, explaining its use to enable IO isolation during low‑power transitions on am43xx platforms.
The patch changes the allocation of the i915 scratch page from device (GT) memory to system memory on every platform, aiming for a uniform configuration and lower device memory usage.

The patch disables allocation of per‑CPU softirq stacks on PREEMPT_RT kernels, because PREEMPT_RT already runs softirqs on the regular kernel stack via __do_softirq(). This removes unused memory usage and guarantees do_softirq_own_stack() is never invoked.
The patch replaces a hand‑written swap operation in the ia64 module code with the generic swap() macro from include/linux/minmax.h, simplifying the implementation without altering functionality.

The patch changes jbd2_submit_inode_data() to invoke the filesystem‑provided j_submit_inode_data_buffers hook instead of the hard‑coded jbd2_journal_submit_inode_data_buffers, letting ext4 fastcommit use ext4_writepages() rather than generic_writepages().
Updates the device‑tree binding documentation for the NXP i.MX8MQ VPU, separating G1 and G2 decoder blocks into distinct nodes that share only the vpu‑blk‑ctrl power domain.
The patch frees the allocated soc_dev_attr structure when of_property_read_string() fails in mxs_machine_init(), preventing a memory leak on error paths.
